title: SentiLab chiplet-placement challenge: the provisional manifest, for learning

status.manifest: provisional draft that uses the design's manifest field names; it is not the signed challenge manifest
status.thresholds: provisional: every threshold is fixed in the signed manifest before any proposal is scored, and never changed in response to outcomes
status.evaluator: gate-zero numerical predicate independently re-derived from signed saved outputs; public scoring not admitted
status.temperatures: provisional model inputs and policy thresholds are distinguished from the saved simulated gate-zero results in /agents/evidence.json; no public proposal result is claimed

label: simulated, steady state, uniform power per die; references reconstructed from published figures; not CAD, not silicon, not measured

design.used_for: manifest field names, legality, the statistic, wire, comparisons, the screen, claim labels and the policy values proposed in the draft (sections 4.1 to 4.11)

brief.used_for: the problems, the rules a layout must follow and how labels are read

contract.used_for: delta_T, q_r, the bounded and screened predicates and the tradeoff budgets

review.used_for: the separation of comparator and published targets, the statistic wording and the scenario-target wording

references.used_for: die sizes, powers and halos, the reference identities and the routed wire of the references

fixture_configs.used_for: the netlists: the files each reference record pins by fixture.config_sha256

problems.name: Ascend 910
problems.description: a shipped AI processor as modelled in the TAP-2.5D paper: the paper's die sizes, powers and connections, not vendor data

fixture.origin: the frame's lower-left corner; +x right, +y up

package.model: TAP-2.5D's 2.5D package model: substrate, C4 bumps, silicon interposer, microbumps, dies, TIM, heat spreader, heat sink
package.assumptions: steady state, uniform power per die

ambient_C.meaning: planned fixed input for the signed manifest; each admitted run binds its actual generated configuration

netlist.entries: R[i][j]: the number of wires between die i and die j

counting.routed: each ordered pair (i, j) with R[i][j] > 0 is a directed net of R[i][j] wires, so each link is routed once in each direction

lattice_um.rationale: a declared finite engineering benchmark choice; not CAD precision, not a manufacturing tolerance, not an uncertainty estimate and not reference-position uncertainty

margin_um.applies_to: each die with its halo, from every frame edge
margin_um.rationale: TAP-2.5D draws edge strips half its 1 mm placement grid wide around the interposer, and every die keeps its halo clear of them

min_die_gap_um.applies_to: die bodies, without halos, along x or along y

legality.halo: each die's microbump ring, from TAP-2.5D's model for the link type: a uniform ring, the same when the die turns; per-die widths in dies[].halo_um. Halo rings may touch but not overlap

statistic.definition: the maximum native centre-map value over the real chiplets enumerated in real_chiplets
statistic.centre_mapping: GRID_CENTER: a die's value is the mean of the 1, 2 or 4 central grid cells of its block on the die layer (pinned)
statistic.not: not a pointwise peak, and never called the true peak
retained_separately: the die layer's hottest grid cell, with its location
the original TAP-2.5D selector, which is not limited to real chiplets
statistic.evaluator: gate-zero numerical predicate independently re-derived from signed saved outputs; public scoring not admitted

wire.definition: the total routed inter-die wirelength in mm from the open router (TAP-2.5D's MILP routing formulation, ported from CPLEX to HiGHS): the routed total reported by HiGHS with optimal status under its numerical tolerances, requesting zero relative MIP gap and using the declared time limit; other solver outcomes leave W UNKNOWN

proxy.definition: the connectivity-weighted mean Manhattan distance between die centres in mm, each unordered pair once
proxy.use: diagnostic only; never used to judge

wire.thermal_solve: none: wire is computed apart from the thermal model

comparator.label: reconstructed from a published figure, continuous, reference-only
comparator.T_R: UNKNOWN: the signed challenge manifest has not admitted this comparator; separate saved gate-zero statistics are in /agents/evidence.json

engineering_variants.label: engineering variant
engineering_variants.role: engineering comparison and sensitivity baseline; never a paper match

published_targets.source: Y. Ma et al., TAP-2.5D, DATE 2021, Fig. 6(a)
published_targets.use: a separately named paper-target diagnostic only; never substituted for T_M(R) or W(R)
published_targets.values: kept in separate fields of the signed manifest; not shown on these pages

policy.status: provisional: policy choices, not uncertainty estimates; fixed in the signed manifest before any proposal is scored

D_K.meaning: D, the allowed thermal degradation: delta_T_upper <= D

r.meaning: the relaxed-wire allowance: q_r_upper <= 0, that is W(c) <= (1 + r) W(R); a relaxed label always names r

B_T_K.meaning: B_T, the required thermal improvement: delta_T_upper <= -B_T

B_W_fraction.basis: references.comparator.W_R_mm, the nominal comparator wire, in every scenario
B_W_fraction.meaning: B_W, the required wire improvement, in mm: this fraction times the nominal W_R_mm (the design's B_W_mm), used as q_0_upper <= -B_W

T_limit_C.meaning: the declared temperature target: a chosen scenario target, not a hardware or safety limit

tradeoff_budgets_r.meaning: nested wire budgets: the best observed T_M under W(c) <= (1 + r) W(R), for each r

bounds.rule: no bound is accepted today, and no bound defaults to zero

scenarios.comparator: the exact perturbed R at grid 64
compared: the routed W of the perturbed R
scenarios.moves: one die, one axis, 500 um either way; every other die and every rotation fixed
scenarios.exclusions: moves that break continuous legality (every fixture rule except the lattice), enumerated before any outcome

screen.basis: B_W stays defined on the nominal W_R_mm in every scenario
screen.rules: the scenarios are fixed before any outcome and never chosen or removed after one; an empty set never passes

layout.entry: one object per die, in the problem's die order, with the fields die, x_um, y_um and rot_deg
layout.coordinates: integer micrometres of the die centre, from the frame's lower-left corner; +x right, +y up
layout.rotation: 0 or 90 degrees about the die centre; a turn swaps width and height; a square die cannot turn

comparisons.comparator: R: the raw reconstruction, scored by the same evaluator and router as the candidate, in the same manifest version; it is continuous and reference-only, so the lattice rule does not apply to it and it is never an entry
comparisons.q_r: W(c) - (1 + r) W(R), in mm; q_r <= 0 means the candidate fits wire allowance r
never: published paper targets in place of T_M(R) or W(R)
T from one geometry with W from another

bounded.u_q(r): b_c + (1 + r) b_R, from individual wire error bounds b_c and b_R, for r >= 0
bounded.status: no bound is accepted today, so u_T, u_q and u_abs are UNKNOWN and no claim is bounded

evidence_modes.bounded: the predicate holds with accepted bounds added (none today)
evidence_modes.passes the listed sensitivity cases: the predicate holds on the estimated values in every required scenario of the screen; not an error bound, and silent about unlisted cases

claims.label: declared temperature target
claims.note: T_limit is a chosen scenario target, not a hardware or safety limit; a centre-mapped value below it says nothing about every die, grid point, junction or real device

claims.label: r-relaxed-wire thermal tolerance
claims.note: r appears in the label; 1.05 times the comparator wire is relaxed, never strict and never equal wire

claims.label: wire improvement with allowed thermal degradation
robust dominance over R
claims.predicate: q_0_upper <= 0 and delta_T_upper <= 0, with at least one strict improvement under the published tie and margin rule

claim_rules: every claim is checked after legality and numerical admission
non-inferiority is not equality, and a two-sided reproduction claim is a different predicate
every result shows its nominal values, labelled or not, INCOMPLETE or not
claims are suppressed by a failed required gate-zero check, a failed source, input or statistic binding, a failed pure predicate fixture or a failed required scenario
an unexpected scientific diagnostic does not suppress valid claims; the mismatch and its raw values are published as a diagnostic
thresholds, scenarios, the evaluator and the reference are never tuned toward expected classifications

claim_states.UNKNOWN: the evidence is missing; never an assumed pass

relaxed.predicate: W(c) <= (1 + r) W(R), with r from policy.r
relaxed.label: relaxed wire, named with its r; never strict and never equal wire

budgets.predicate: W(c) <= (1 + r) W(R) for each r in policy.tradeoff_budgets_r
budgets.label: within the r wire budget
budgets.rules: nested, so one layout can appear in several; wire-budget scenarios, not weights or tracks; not separate wins and not evidence of global optimality; more wire without a temperature benefit is not a tradeoff

definitions.tradeoff: for each budget r, report the best observed T_M under W(c) <= (1 + r) W(R); strict, relaxed and nondominated results are reported separately
definitions.pareto: the nondominated set of T_M against W, with no claim
